chunks: And from him, from Zura'ah ibn Muhammad, from Sama'ah, from Abu Basir and Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, both of them from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"Whoever performs the ritual bath (ghusl) before the rising of dawn, having already performed the full bath (istihmam) before that, and then enters the state of Ihram on that day, his ghusl suffices for him. And if he bathed at the beginning of the night and then entered Ihram at the end of the night, his ghusl suffices for him."
As for if he slept after the bath before contracting the Ihram, then it is obligatory upon him to repeat the bath. He narrated that.

key_terms.أَحْرَمَ: Entered the state of Ihram (sacred ritual status)

ai.seo_question: Does sleeping after the ritual bath invalidate the ghusl for Hajj Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the temporal validity of the ritual bath (ghusl) for Ihram, distinguishing between mere passage of time and the act of sleep which nullifies the state of purity. It highlights the scholarly principle that sleep breaks the continuity of ritual purity, requiring a fresh ghusl if one sleeps before formally entering the state of Ihram, a nuance critical for pilgrims ensuring their worship is valid according to Ja'fari jurisprudence.
